tasks.description: Load the CSV, parse timestamps to datetime, enforce float types for temperature and humidity, and verify 5-minute sampling intervals.
Compute Humidex from temperature and relative humidity and assign comfort categories (e.g., comfortable, some discomfort, great discomfort).
Calculate Thom’s Discomfort Index (DI) using temperature and humidity and label comfort risk levels.
Detect anomalies in temperature_c and humidity_percent using a rolling z-score (window=5); flag readings where |z| > 2.5 and output flagged timestamps with z-scores.
Monitor 5-minute deltas and flag sudden changes when |Δtemperature_c| > 0.7°C or |Δhumidity_percent| > 3.0% in a single interval.
Resample to hourly bins and compute mean, min, max, std, and count for temperature_c and humidity_percent to produce compact hourly summaries.
Compute dew_point_c per reading using the Magnus-Tetens formula (a=17.62, b=243.12) from temperature_c and humidity_percent.
Estimate absolute humidity (g/m^3) per reading using temperature_c and humidity_percent via saturation vapor pressure-based calculation.
Predict next 60-minute average temperature and humidity using simple exponential smoothing (alpha=0.3) on 5-minute data; output mean forecast and an approximate ±1σ uncertainty from residuals.
Trigger alerts when temperature_c > 30.0°C or humidity_percent > 65.0% for at least 2 consecutive readings; include start time, end time, and duration.
Detect potential sensor lock-up by checking if rolling std over the last 6 readings is < 0.05°C for temperature or < 0.5% for humidity; flag the period as suspect.

Estimate wet-bulb temperature (°C) per reading using Stull’s empirical formula from temperature_c and humidity_percent; output WBT and simple heat stress bands (e.g., <20 safe, 20–24 caution, 24–26 high caution, >26 danger).

Compute saturation vapor pressure (es) from temperature_c (Magnus), actual vapor pressure (ea = es * RH/100), and VPD = es - ea (kPa); classify humidity dryness bands (<0.6 humid, 0.6–1.2 moderate, >1.2 dry).
Accumulate degree-minutes above a configurable comfort setpoint (default 26.0°C) using 5-minute intervals: sum(max(0, temperature_c - setpoint) * 5) to quantify overheating burden.

Compute percent of time within a simplified comfort box (temperature_c in [22, 26] and humidity_percent in [30, 60]); report compliance %, compliant minutes, and longest continuous non-compliance streak.

Detect monotonic ramp events where temperature_c increases by ≥0.2°C per step for ≥3 consecutive readings or humidity_percent increases by ≥1.0% per step; output start/end timestamps and total change.
Apply one-sided CUSUM to humidity_percent to flag sustained upward drift (e.g., k=0.5, h=3.0 in % units); return drift start/end times and peak CUSUM.

Compute dewpoint depression (temperature_c − dew_point_c) and classify condensation risk (high <2°C, moderate 2–4°C, low >4°C); optionally flag if dew_point_c ≥ (temperature_c − 2.0) to indicate potential surface condensation.
Calculate rolling Pearson correlation (window=6) and overall correlation between temperature_c and humidity_percent; flag windows where |corr| > 0.6 as strong coupling periods.
Using a linear fit on the last N readings (default N=6), estimate minutes until temperature_c > 30.0°C or humidity_percent > 65.0% if the slope is positive; output predicted breach time or None.
